_readme: The portal list. This file is the source of truth for which portals exist,
what they are called, whether they are enabled, and where they are read from.
Validated on load by portal_config.py: a malformed entry names itself, is
skipped, and is reported as unavailable in the run's portal status table. It
An entry with no 'module' is data alone. It is read through the same
six-layer extraction cascade every HTML portal uses: feed, embedded JSON,
CSS selectors, header-aware tables, structural inference, anchor pattern.
That is enough for many listings from a URL alone -- and it is best-effort,
not a guarantee. The quality score and row count from the first run say
An entry with a 'module' has bespoke fetch logic in portals/<module>.py --
a POST search endpoint or a REST API, not a page. Its 'code_owned' fields
are set in that module, and setting them here is rejected rather than
Why each portal is configured the way it is: PORTALS.md.

portals.name: World Bank
portals.notes: REST API. Offset paging, the country-field test that beats the API's own full-text search, and the notice-id link are all in portals/worldbank.py.

portals.name: EU TED
portals.notes: REST API with its own query grammar: the country is the three-letter code JOR and the page limit is 100. Both were 400s until they were fixed. portals/ted.py.

portals.name: SAM.gov (USAID / US Gov)
portals.notes: REST API needing a free key (SAM_API_KEY) whose approval takes 1-4 weeks. Without it the portal reports 'not configured', which is deliberately not the same as 'unavailable'. portals/samgov.py.

portals.name: UK Find a Tender
portals.notes: OCDS API over the whole UK corpus, which is why country matching is on word boundaries -- Jordanstown and Ammanford are in it. portals/fcdo.py.

portals.name: UNGM (UNDP, UNICEF, WFP, UNOPS, UNHCR, UNRWA)
portals.notes: The richest Jordan source. Its rows come from a POST search endpoint filtered to Jordan and paged to the end, not from this URL, which is 141 KB of pure navigation. The selectors and the sibling-span field selectors were derived from the live DOM and carry their reasoning in portals/ungm.py; editing them here would be ignored, so it is rejected.

portals.name: EBRD
portals.notes: ebrd.com plus ECEPP; ECEPP carries the consultancy assignments. Verified live: 4,012 notices scanned, 119 Jordan.

portals.name: EIB
portals.notes: Corporate and project procurement in one listing. Returns a bot wall from a data-centre IP; the selectors are unverified.

portals.name: GIZ
portals.notes: The German ausschreibungen portal, verified live at quality 1.00. giz.de/en/partner/contractor/tenders was removed after --capture showed it carries no listing at all -- its repeated blocks were the main menu.

portals.name: KfW (via Germany Trade & Invest)
portals.notes: KfW does NOT publish tender notices on kfw.de -- Germany Trade & Invest is entrusted with them. Pointing this at kfw.de would make the portal report unavailable forever while looking like an honest failure.

portals.name: IsDB
portals.notes: Jordan is a member country. Member-country restrictions are flagged by the eligibility detector, never dropped. Read cleanly live: 144 notices, no open Jordan ones that day.

portals.name: Saudi Fund for Development
portals.notes: Arabic and English. Saudi-firm restrictions are flagged, not excluded -- a JV route may still be open. Times out from a data-centre IP.

portals.name: Abu Dhabi Fund for Development
portals.no_listing_reason: ADFD's tenders page carries no listing (rendered or not); its financed tenders are issued by the beneficiary government.
portals.notes: Four URLs and two fetch strategies, including a real browser, all returned chrome and zero rows. anchor_hint is deliberately absent: pinning it to /News/ silently excluded every tender link. See PORTALS.md.

portals.name: JICA
portals.no_listing_reason: JICA's Jordan office has no procurement page; its notices, when there are any, appear on the office index or via the Ministry of Planning.
portals.notes: Both URL spellings 404 today, while Bangladesh and Indonesia answer on both -- so this is not a broken scraper and no URL will fix it. The office index was tried and removed: it put two of its own section headings in the report as tenders. Every source here must be a procurement page, not an index.
